chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is from the Sunnah and the righteousness that a man should be known by his father's name (teknonymy).

key_terms.يُكَنَّى: To be known by a kunya (teknonym)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on using a father's name for teknonymy?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi elevates teknonymy to a recommended act of 'Birr' (righteousness), linking personal identity directly to familial honor and social respect. It reflects the broader Islamic emphasis on preserving lineage and maintaining clear social structures, where a man is distinguished by his father's name as a mark of dignity and continuity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘(It is) from the Sunnah and the righteousness that the man should teknonym himself with the name of his father’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
It is of tradition and virtue to adopt al-Kunyah (like abu’ meaning father of or ‘Ibn’) of the name of one’s father.’”
